official.deadline_note: The 2026 call states the closing date as six weeks from its publication date of 18 January 2026; no 2027 deadline has been published.
official.application_cycle: 2026 Overseas MSc and PhD award cycle (award lists published as the 2026/2027 UK-Split Site and Germany, France and Malaysia (GFM) Strategic Partnership Scholarships)
official.status_note: The most recent Overseas Scheme call, published 18 January 2026, closed on 27 February 2026. PTDF published the lists of 2026/2027 GFM awardees on 27 May 2026. As of 10 October 2026 the portal news index shows no newly opened Overseas call.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Scholarship Benefits: 'Tuition and bench fees (where applicable)'
benefits: Allowances for accommodation and living expenses
eligibility: MSc applicants must possess a minimum of Second Class Upper (2:1) in the first degree, or a Second Class Lower (2:2) with relevant industry experience
PhD applicants must possess at least Second Class Lower (2:2) in the first degree and a good postgraduate degree
Have completed the mandatory National Youth Service Corps (NYSC)
Possess five (5) O-Level credits, including English Language and Mathematics
Have a National Identity Number (NIN) and ensure it is fully verified prior to application (NIMC verification charges apply)
All lecturers must submit a letter from their Vice-Chancellors confirming that they are not currently benefiting from any other scholarship
requirements: Applications are limited to PTDF-approved courses at PTDF partner institutions
Scholarships will only be awarded for studies relevant to PTDF's mandate; candidates may be disqualified for programmes deemed not relevant to the oil and gas industry
The proposed course of study must be consistent with the applicant's prior academic background

MSc applicants must submit a Statement of Purpose (maximum 500 words) covering rationale for the proposed study, relevance to the oil and gas industry, and expected contribution to national development
PhD applicants must submit a research proposal relevant to the oil and gas industry (maximum five pages) covering topic, introduction/background, objectives, methodology, and data collection approach

For the 2026 academic year, UK PhD scholarships are limited to split-site programmes at the College of Petroleum and Energy Studies, Kaduna (CPESK) with Robert Gordon University, University of Strathclyde or University of Portsmouth
PhD applicants intending to apply under the PTDF/DAAD partnership in Germany must secure a research supervisor prior to the final selection interviews
Multiple applications will result in automatic disqualification
Submission of any illegible or falsified documents will result in automatic disqualification
Candidates previously sponsored by the Fund for a scholarship category (MSc/PhD) are ineligible to apply again for the same or lower category
Shortlisted candidates invited for interview will be required to present their transcripts
documents: First Degree Certificate or Statement of Result
WAEC/GCE/SSCE/NECO results and the relevant PIN(s) to enable online verification
Evidence of membership of relevant professional associations
selection_criteria: Academic merit (quality of degrees, complete academic transcripts, and relevant professional qualifications)
Viability and relevance of the study plan / research proposal
Relevance of prior studies to the oil and gas industry and the proposed programme/research
coverage: Allowances for accommodation and living expenses
application_method: Create an applicant account on the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal at scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng
Complete and submit the online application form, scanning and uploading clear copies of the mandatory documents
Following initial screening based on submitted qualifications, the top applicants in each category from each State are invited for an interview where transcripts must be presented
official.application_route: Apply online through the PTDF Scholarship Management Portal (scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng) to approved programmes at PTDF partner universities; shortlisted candidates are invited to a selection interview.
official.citizenship_residency: Nigerian citizens; a Local Government Identification Letter (evidence of state of origin and local government) is a mandatory upload, and shortlisting is done for the top applicants in each category from each State.
official.international_eligibility: Open to Nigerian citizens only; the sponsored study takes place at PTDF partner universities in the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Malaysia.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Only PTDF-approved courses at PTDF partner institutions; scholarships are awarded only for studies relevant to PTDF's mandate in the oil and gas industry, and the course must be consistent with the applicant's prior academic background.
official.research_requirement: PhD applicants must submit a research proposal relevant to the oil and gas industry of maximum five pages; PhD applicants under the PTDF/DAAD partnership in Germany must secure a research supervisor prior to the final selection interviews.
official.description: The Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), a Federal Government agency responsible for developing indigenous human capacity and petroleum technology for Nigeria's oil and gas sector, invites applications for its Overseas MSc and PhD Scholarships to study specific programmes at selected partner universities in the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Malaysia. The award includes return flight tickets, health insurance, payment of tuition and bench fees (where applicable), and allowances to meet the costs of accommodation and living expenses.

applicant_utility.summary: PTDF covers tuition and bench fees, return flights, health insurance and accommodation/living allowances for MSc and PhD study at partner universities in the UK, Germany, France and Malaysia, but only for courses it pre-approves each year. The call runs for just six weeks from publication and the 2026 round closed on 27 February 2026, so the practical move is to prepare documents now and watch the portal news page. Selection is interview-based and state-by-state, so a clean transcript plus a study plan explicitly tied to Nigeria's oil and gas sector outweighs applying broadly.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Nigerian graduates holding at least a 2:1 in an oil-and-gas-related first degree (or a 2:2 plus relevant industry experience for MSc) who have completed NYSC and want a funded MSc or PhD abroad.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify your NIN through the portal before the call opens and keep the payment reference; NIMC verification charges apply and the portal has posted maintenance notices for this step
Buy and keep valid WAEC/GCE/SSCE/NECO result PINs so PTDF can verify your O-Level credits online during screening
Request signed and stamped transcripts early, because shortlisted candidates must present them at interview on short notice
Draft the MSc Statement of Purpose (max 500 words) or PhD research proposal (max five pages) around oil and gas relevance, objectives, methodology and data collection
Match your intended programme to the current approved course list at partner institutions before starting the form
Lecturers should obtain the Vice-Chancellor letter confirming no concurrent scholarship in advance
PTDF/DAAD Germany PhD applicants should identify and secure a prospective research supervisor before final interviews are called
common_rejection_risks: Submitting more than one application or duplicate account, which is an automatic disqualification
Uploading illegible or falsified documents, also an automatic disqualification
Choosing a programme PTDF deems irrelevant to the oil and gas industry, including courses outside the approved list
Proposing a study path inconsistent with your prior academic background
Having been previously sponsored by PTDF in the same (MSc) or a higher category
Unverified NIN or missing O-Level PINs, which stall the application before screening
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: PTDF publishes no monetary value for its allowances, so budget for items not listed as covered: NIMC NIN verification charges, WAEC/NECO result PINs, transcript procurement, visa and biometric fees, and any family or personal costs beyond the accommodation and living allowances.
document_audit: O-Level results need the actual PINs for online verification, so expired scratch cards are a real trap
A Statement of Result is accepted in place of a First Degree Certificate, which helps applicants still awaiting certificate release
The NYSC Discharge Certificate is mandatory for both MSc and PhD applicants
The Local Government Identification Letter must evidence state of origin and local government
The Master's certificate is required only from PhD applicants; membership evidence of professional associations is required from everyone
Transcripts are not uploaded with the application but must be producible at the interview stage
alerts: The 2026 call (published 18 January 2026) closed on 27 February 2026 and the 2026/2027 award lists were published on 27 May 2026; no new Overseas call was open as of 10 October 2026, and past windows have opened in either January or April and lasted only six weeks
For 2026, UK PhD places are split-site only, shared between CPESK Kaduna and Robert Gordon University, the University of Strathclyde or the University of Portsmouth
Germany PhD applicants under the PTDF/DAAD partnership must have a research supervisor secured before the final selection interviews
Do not create a second account to reapply within the same cycle, as multiple applications are an automatic disqualification
Benefits are published as categories rather than a fixed stipend, so do not rely on any specific monthly figure quoted by third-party sites
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create a portal account, verify your NIN (paid), complete the online form and upload the mandatory documents, then state-and-category screening leads to an interview where transcripts are presented, followed by publication of award lists.
